sentences: She migrated to Australia on a skilled visa — her engineering qualifications were in demand.
He found the skilled visa pathway the most common route for professional migrants to Australia.
A skilled visa allows migrants with occupation-specific qualifications to live and work in Australia.
She found the skilled visa requiring a skills assessment from the relevant Australian authority.
He found the skilled visa points test considering age, English proficiency, work experience, and qualifications.
Skilled visas include the subclass 189, 190, and 491 — each with different conditions.
She found the Skilled Occupation List determining which roles were eligible for each visa subclass.
He found the skilled visa process taking between six months and two years — patience required.
Skilled visa holders can often include partner and dependent children in their application.
She describes the skilled visa as the document that most changed the trajectory of her family's life.
She applied for a partner visa to join her Australian husband — the process was thorough.
He found the partner visa requiring substantial evidence of a genuine relationship.
A partner visa allows the spouse or de facto partner of an Australian citizen or permanent resident to live in Australia.
She found the partner visa application requiring statutory declarations, photos, joint financial documents.
He found the partner visa granted in two stages — a temporary visa first, then a permanent one.
Partner visas include the onshore subclass 820/801 and the offshore subclass 309/100.
She found the partner visa among the most emotionally complex processes — uncertainty for months.
He found the partner visa requiring evidence over the life of the relationship — not just a marriage certificate.
Partner visa processing times vary — currently measured in months to years depending on caseload.
She describes the partner visa as the most painstaking administrative process she had ever completed — and the most worth it.
She arrived in Australia on a student visa — four years studying and working.
He found the student visa allowing part-time work — up to forty-eight hours per fortnight during study.
A student visa — subclass 500 — allows international students to study full-time at an Australian institution.
She found the student visa requiring enrolment confirmation from an approved education provider.
He found the student visa holder able to include family members as secondary applicants.
Student visas in Australia require health insurance — Overseas Student Health Cover.
She found the student visa granting work rights — critical for financial sustainability.
He found the student visa expiring with the course end date — he planned his next step in advance.
Student visas can lead to post-study work visas — the Temporary Graduate Visa subclass 485.
She describes the student visa period as the four years that most shaped who she became.
She submitted her visa application through the Department of Home Affairs online portal.
He found the Department of Home Affairs managing migration, citizenship, and border security.
The Department of Home Affairs is the Australian government body responsible for immigration and citizenship.
She found the Home Affairs website — homeaffairs.gov.au — the primary source for migration information.
He found the Department of Home Affairs processing timelines published and updated regularly.
The Department of Home Affairs replaced the Department of Immigration in 2017.
She found the Home Affairs ImmiAccount system the portal for all visa applications and tracking.
He found the Department of Home Affairs also responsible for the Australian Federal Police and ASIO.
The Department of Home Affairs processes millions of visa applications and travel movements annually.
She describes navigating the Department of Home Affairs website as the skill she most wished had been taught to her before she applied.
She hired a migration agent after her visa application was refused — professional advice made a difference.
He found a registered migration agent essential for complex visa cases.
A migration agent provides advice, assistance, and representation in Australian immigration matters.
She found migration agents required to be registered with the OMARA — Office of the Migration Agents Registration Authority.
He found migration agent fees varying widely — fixed fee per application or hourly rate.
Migration agents in Australia must meet educational and ethical requirements set by OMARA.
She found checking OMARA registration the most important step before engaging a migration agent.
He found the migration agent navigating the regulatory complexity his research had not fully captured.
Migration agents differ from immigration lawyers — though both can assist with complex matters.
She describes her migration agent as the professional whose knowledge saved her significant time and distress.
She checked the MARA register before engaging any migration agent.
He found MARA registration the minimum requirement for a legitimate migration agent.
MARA stands for the Migration Agents Registration Authority — now called OMARA.
She found the MARA register searchable by name or registration number at mara.gov.au.
He found a MARA-registered agent required to follow a Code of Conduct and maintain professional development.
MARA registration ensures clients have recourse if an agent behaves improperly.
She found the MARA complaints process available if an agent acted unethically or incompetently.
He warned a friend about unlicensed migration advice — only engage a MARA-registered professional.
MARA registration must be renewed annually — she checked the expiry date of her agent's registration.
She describes the MARA register as the thirty-second check that protected a multi-thousand-dollar decision.
She sat the IELTS exam three times before achieving the band score required for her visa.
He found IELTS the most widely accepted English language test for Australian immigration.
IELTS stands for International English Language Testing System — accepted for migration, study, and registration.
She found the IELTS test comprising four components: listening, reading, writing, and speaking.
He found the IELTS band score ranging from one to nine — most skilled visas requiring six point five or above.
IELTS Academic and IELTS General Training differ — migration uses General Training in most cases.
She found IELTS preparation courses available through TAFE and private providers.
He found IELTS results valid for two years from the test date — timing his application carefully.
IELTS test centres operate in most Australian cities and major international cities.
She describes IELTS preparation as the most structured English study she had ever done — and the most useful.
She completed her NAATI certification to work as an accredited interpreter in Australia.
He found NAATI-certified interpreters required for legal, medical, and immigration proceedings.
NAATI stands for the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.
She found NAATI certification offering extra points in the skilled migration points test.
He found NAATI certification requiring an examination in both English and the target language.
NAATI certification is Australia's quality standard for professional translators and interpreters.
She found NAATI-certified translation required for all documents submitted with a visa application.
He found certified NAATI translators listed on the NAATI website — searchable by language.
NAATI certification levels include Certified Translator, Certified Interpreter, and specialised credentials.
She describes earning NAATI certification as the professional achievement that most valued both her languages.
She requested an interpreter for the medical appointment — her English improved but technical language still challenged her.
He found interpreters available through the Translating and Interpreting Service at no cost.
An interpreter converts spoken language from one language to another in real time.
She found the TIS National service — Translating and Interpreting Service — available twenty-four hours.
He found interpreters available by telephone, video, and in person depending on the service.
Interpreters are distinct from translators — interpreters work with spoken language; translators with written.
She found interpreter services required for legal hearings, medical consultations, and government appointments.
He found the interpreter at the hospital visit invaluable — accuracy mattered more than comfort there.
Interpreters must be impartial — they relay what is said, not what they think should be said.
She describes finding a professional interpreter as the difference between receiving and missing the information that mattered most.
She called TIS National before her GP appointment — free interpreting for eligible services.
He found TIS National providing phone and video interpreting in over one hundred and fifty languages.
TIS National is the Australian government's Translating and Interpreting Service.
She found TIS National accessible at 131 450 — around the clock, every day of the year.
He found TIS National providing free interpreting for calls to Australian government services.
TIS National interpreters are professionally trained and operate under a code of ethics.
She found TIS National used by Medicare, Centrelink, and many health and community organisations.
He found TIS National able to connect an interpreter within minutes for most major languages.
TIS National also provides pre-booked on-site interpreting for planned appointments.
She describes TIS National as the service that most removed the barrier between her language and Australian systems.
She experienced culture shock in her first months — the casualness caught her off guard.
He found culture shock affecting even highly educated, well-prepared migrants.
Culture shock is the disorientation experienced when encountering an unfamiliar culture.
She found culture shock manifesting as fatigue, irritability, and homesickness — all at once.
He found culture shock following a predictable arc: honeymoon, frustration, adjustment, acceptance.
Culture shock in Australia often centres on informality, directness, and social norms around personal space.
She found acknowledging culture shock rather than suppressing it the most effective response.
He found fellow migrants describing culture shock years after arrival — it did not always resolve quickly.
Culture shock affects relationships, work performance, and wellbeing — support helps.
She describes culture shock as the uncomfortable teacher that most accelerated her understanding of Australia.
She found the Turkish diaspora in Melbourne warm, organised, and connected.
He found the diaspora community providing the most immediate welcome when he arrived.
A diaspora is a community of people living outside their country of origin who maintain cultural connection.
She found diaspora communities in Australia among the most culturally vibrant in the world.
He found the diaspora network accelerating his job search — referrals within the community.
Australia has significant diaspora communities from China, India, Lebanon, Italy, Greece, and many more.
She found the diaspora community a source of comfort when homesickness became overwhelming.
He found diaspora cultural associations organising events, language schools, and welfare support.
Diaspora remittances — money sent home — form a significant portion of income in some countries.
She describes her diaspora community as the bridge she most depended on between two worlds.
She cried at her citizenship ceremony — four years of work and waiting culminating in one room.
He found the citizenship ceremony held at the local council chambers on Australia Day or another date.
A citizenship ceremony is the formal event at which applicants become Australian citizens.
She found the citizenship ceremony requiring her to make the Australian Citizenship Pledge.
He found the citizenship ceremony a community event — family invited, local Mayor presiding.
Citizenship ceremonies in Australia are held by local councils on behalf of the federal government.
She found the ceremony unexpectedly moving — the room full of people from dozens of countries.
He found the citizenship ceremony confirming rights to vote, hold an Australian passport, and access all benefits.
Citizenship ceremony invitations arrive after the citizenship application is approved.
She describes the citizenship ceremony as the most significant public moment of her adult life.
She received her permanent residency grant five years after her initial arrival.
He found permanent residency unlocking access to Medicare, university fee rates, and work rights.
Permanent residency is a visa status allowing a person to live in Australia indefinitely without being a citizen.
She found permanent residency required before applying for citizenship in most pathways.
He found permanent residents able to work, study, and access most government services.
Permanent residency in Australia can be granted through skilled, family, and humanitarian pathways.
She found permanent residency a visa — not citizenship — and respected the distinction.
He found permanent residents required to meet residency obligations to maintain their status.
Permanent residency opens the path to citizenship after four years — including one as a permanent resident.
She describes receiving permanent residency as the day that most made Australia feel like home in legal and emotional terms.
She applied for Australian citizenship after four years as a permanent resident.
He found Australian citizenship requiring a test, a ceremony, and demonstrated knowledge of Australia.
Australian citizenship provides full rights — the vote, the passport, and the deepest sense of belonging.
She found Australian citizenship requiring four years of lawful residence, one as a permanent resident.
He found the citizenship test covering Australian values, history, and government.
Australian citizenship can be acquired by birth, adoption, or grant — she received hers by grant.
She found Australian citizenship allowing dual citizenship in most cases — she kept her original passport.
He found the citizenship application fee significant — worth every cent for what it unlocked.
Australian citizenship carries responsibilities: to vote, respect the law, and participate in the community.
She describes Australian citizenship as the status that most fully expressed her commitment to her new country.
She reported discrimination to the Australian Human Rights Commission after the incident at work.
He found discrimination law in Australia covering race, sex, age, disability, and other grounds.
Discrimination is the unfair or prejudicial treatment of a person based on a protected characteristic.
She found the Racial Discrimination Act 1975 the primary federal protection against racial discrimination.
He found discrimination complaints handled at the federal level by the AHRC and state level by local bodies.
Discrimination can be direct — treating someone less favourably — or indirect — an apparently neutral rule that disadvantages.
She found workplace discrimination the most commonly reported form in Australian surveys.
He found discrimination in housing, education, and service provision also illegal under Australian law.
She found legal advice at the community legal centre helpful in understanding her options.
She describes speaking up about discrimination as the most difficult and necessary thing she had done in Australia.
She lodged a complaint with the Australian Human Rights Commission after being dismissed unfairly.
He found the Australian Human Rights Commission investigating complaints about discrimination and human rights breaches.
The Australian Human Rights Commission — AHRC — is Australia's national human rights institution.
She found the AHRC providing a free conciliation service for discrimination complaints.
He found the AHRC publishing reports, guidelines, and resources on human rights in Australia.
The AHRC handles complaints under federal discrimination laws — race, sex, disability, and age.
She found the AHRC complaint process beginning with a written lodgement — no fee required.
He found the AHRC Commissioner conducting public inquiries into systemic human rights issues.
The AHRC can conciliate but not adjudicate — unresolved complaints can proceed to the Federal Court.
She describes lodging with the AHRC as the formal act that most restored her sense that rules applied to everyone.
She watches SBS news each evening — the international coverage is the most thorough she has found.
He found SBS broadcasting in over sixty languages — the most multilingual free-to-air channel in Australia.
SBS — the Special Broadcasting Service — is Australia's multicultural and multilingual public broadcaster.
She found SBS World News providing the most internationally comprehensive Australian free-to-air news.
He found SBS On Demand streaming films and series in languages not found on other platforms.
SBS was established in 1977 to serve Australia's multicultural communities.
She found SBS Food — the dedicated food channel — a daily companion during her first year.
He found SBS language radio broadcasting to communities across the country.
SBS is funded by the Australian government but editorially independent.
She describes SBS as the broadcaster that most made her feel Australian media was speaking to her.
She sends her children to a community language school on Saturdays — she wants them to keep Turkish.
He found community language schools supported by the Victorian and New South Wales governments.
A community language school teaches heritage or ethnic languages to children outside of school hours.
She found community language schools operating on weekends — Saturday morning was the most common.
He found his daughter's community language school teaching language alongside cultural traditions.
Community language schools in Australia serve over one hundred different language communities.
She found the community language school building bilingualism — a cognitive and cultural advantage.
He found community language schools run by volunteer community organisations with government funding.
Community language schools are registered with state education departments for funding eligibility.
She describes the community language school as the weekly investment that most protected what she did not want her children to lose.
She found multiculturalism a foundational Australian policy — not just a social description.
He found Australian multiculturalism meaning that cultural diversity was valued, not merely tolerated.
Multiculturalism is a policy and social approach in which multiple cultures coexist and are respected.
She found Australian multiculturalism dating to the 1970s policy shift away from assimilation.
He found the Galbally Report of 1978 shaping Australia's multiculturalism framework.
Multiculturalism in Australia supports cultural expression while requiring commitment to shared civic values.
She found the Australian Multicultural Framework guiding government policy across portfolios.
He found multiculturalism contested in public debate — its meaning and limits regularly discussed.
Multiculturalism in practice is visible in language services, multicultural media, and community programs.
She describes Australian multiculturalism as the policy that most clearly explained why she was welcomed — and what she was welcomed into.
She volunteered at the refugee welcome centre — helping families with their first week of settlement.
He found the refugee definition in international law specific — persecution, not poverty.
A refugee is a person who has fled their country due to persecution, war, or violence.
She found Australia accepting refugees through the humanitarian program — an annual cap set by government.
He found the Refugee Convention of 1951 the international framework Australia was party to.
Refugees in Australia receive settlement support through AMES Australia and other providers.
She found the refugee experience in Australia widely varied — family background, country of origin, support.
He found the refugee community contributing enormously to Australian business and public life over generations.
Refugees are distinct from asylum seekers — refugee status is formally recognised by UNHCR or a government.
She describes meeting refugees as the encounters that most expanded her understanding of resilience and loss.
She found the distinction between asylum seeker and refugee legally significant in Australia.
He found asylum seekers awaiting a determination of their refugee status — not yet formally recognised.
An asylum seeker is a person who has applied for refugee status and is awaiting a decision.
She found Australian asylum seeker policy among the most debated immigration issues in the country.
He found asylum seekers entitled to legal advice and basic support while their claims were assessed.
Asylum seekers in Australia may come by air or sea — processing conditions differed significantly.
She found the Asylum Seeker Resource Centre in Melbourne providing support, food, and legal advice.
He found the asylum seeker community including people from the Middle East, Sri Lanka, and Afghanistan.
Asylum seekers are protected by international law from being returned to danger — non-refoulement.
She describes working with asylum seekers as the experience that most challenged her to understand the legal and human weight of a border.
She found the settlement process in Australia supported by government-funded agencies.
He found settlement the most personally demanding period of his migration — more than the application.
Settlement refers to the process of establishing a new life in a country after migration.
She found settlement support including English classes, housing assistance, and employment pathways.
He found the settlement period taking between two and five years for most migrants — an honest timeline.
Settlement services in Australia are provided through the AMEP — Adult Migrant English Program.
She found her settlement caseworker the most practically useful professional in her first year.
He found settlement shaped by employment — finding work was the accelerant for everything else.
Settlement outcomes vary significantly depending on language proficiency, qualifications, and social networks.
She describes the settlement period as the most demanding and most defining chapter of her Australian story.
She enrolled in AMEP as soon as she arrived — five hundred hours of free English tuition.
He found the Adult Migrant English Program the most accessible English program for new arrivals.
The Adult Migrant English Program — AMEP — provides free English language tuition to eligible migrants.
She found AMEP classes offered at flexible times — including evenings for those working during the day.
He found AMEP expanding entitlement — eligible migrants can now access unlimited tuition.
The Adult Migrant English Program is funded by the Australian federal government.
She found AMEP classes covering not just English but Australian workplace culture and everyday life.
He found AMEP delivered through TAFE institutions, private providers, and community organisations.
AMEP includes a home tutor program — volunteers providing one-on-one English practice.
She describes AMEP as the program that most bridged the gap between arriving in Australia and belonging here.

words.meaning: Avustralya'nın önde gelen göçmen ve mülteci destek kuruluşu
sentences: She received settlement support through AMES Australia after arriving as a humanitarian entrant.
He found AMES Australia the largest provider of settlement services in the country.
AMES Australia is a social enterprise providing settlement, employment, and language services to migrants.
She found AMES Australia providing English training, job placement, and community orientation.
He found AMES Australia operating across Victoria and delivering programs nationally.
AMES Australia serves humanitarian entrants, skilled migrants, and international students.
She found AMES Australia's Community Connections program pairing new arrivals with established volunteers.
He found the AMES Australia employment service the fastest path to his first Australian job.
AMES Australia publishes research and policy papers on migration and settlement outcomes.
She describes AMES Australia as the organisation that most practically supported the first and hardest year.
She purchased Overseas Student Health Cover before her student visa was granted — it is mandatory.
He found OSHC a visa requirement for international students in Australia.
Overseas Student Health Cover — OSHC — is compulsory health insurance for international students in Australia.
She found OSHC covering GP visits, hospital treatment, and some specialist care.
He found OSHC premiums varying by provider — Medibank, Bupa, and others offer it.
OSHC does not cover all medical expenses — she read the product disclosure statement carefully.
She found OSHC typically purchased through the university at enrolment.
He found OSHC covering ambulance services — unlike some domestic health insurance.
OSHC runs for the duration of the student visa — she extended it when her course was extended.
She describes OSHC as the insurance she was relieved to have the first time she needed a doctor.
She came to Australia on a working holiday visa — six months of travel, work, and exploration.
He found the working holiday visa available to citizens of many countries aged eighteen to thirty.
A working holiday visa — subclass 417 or 462 — allows young people to work and travel in Australia.
She found the working holiday visa restricting employment to six months with a single employer.
He found a second working holiday visa available after completing regional work — farming, harvesting.
Working holiday visa holders are among the most important seasonal workers in Australian agriculture.
She found the working holiday visa the most common first entry point for young migrants.
He found the working holiday visa renewable through regional, construction, or bushfire recovery work.
Working holiday visa holders can study for up to four months as part of the visa.
She describes the working holiday visa year as the experience that most unexpectedly became the beginning of the rest of her life.
She applied for a Temporary Graduate Visa after completing her master's degree.
He found the Temporary Graduate Visa allowing post-study work rights for up to four years.
The Temporary Graduate Visa — subclass 485 — allows international graduates to work in Australia after study.
She found the Temporary Graduate Visa duration depending on the level and location of study.
He found graduates who studied in regional areas receiving longer Temporary Graduate Visas.
The Temporary Graduate Visa requires a skills assessment in some streams.
She found the Temporary Graduate Visa the bridge from student visa to skilled migration.
He found the Temporary Graduate Visa enabling him to gain Australian work experience before applying for permanent residency.
The Temporary Graduate Visa is not renewable — she planned her permanent pathway well before it expired.
She describes the Temporary Graduate Visa as the most valuable years of professional development she received.

words.meaning: puan testi (göçmenlik başvurusunda kullanılan puan sistemi)
sentences: She maximised her points test score through English study, regional nomination, and her age advantage.
He found the points test the central mechanism of Australia's skilled migration system.
The points test is a scoring system used to assess skilled migration applicants — higher scores receive invitations first.
She found the points test awarding points for age, qualifications, English proficiency, and work experience.
He found the minimum points test score required at sixty-five — competitive scores much higher.
The points test is administered through the SkillSelect system — applicants submit expressions of interest.
She found NAATI certification adding five extra points to her points test score.
He found state nomination worth an additional five points — he pursued it actively.
Points test scores are compared across all applicants — invitations issued to highest scorers.
She describes understanding the points test as the knowledge that most clarified her migration pathway.
She lodged her Expression of Interest through SkillSelect and waited for an invitation.
He found SkillSelect the online system managing skilled migration applications in Australia.
SkillSelect is the platform through which skilled migration applicants submit expressions of interest.
She found SkillSelect drawing down applicants by points score in invitation rounds.
He found invitation rounds through SkillSelect occurring regularly — every two weeks for some streams.
SkillSelect manages subclass 189, 190, and 491 visa streams.
She found her SkillSelect profile requiring accurate skills assessment and occupation codes.
He found the SkillSelect cut-off point varying each round — competitive in high-demand occupations.
SkillSelect replaced the old queue system — it prioritises applicants by score, not application date.
She describes SkillSelect as the system that most transparently showed her where she stood in the migration queue.
She applied for state nomination from Victoria — it added five points and opened a faster pathway.
He found state nomination requiring the applicant to commit to living in the nominating state.
State nomination is an endorsement by an Australian state or territory that supports a skilled migration application.
She found state nomination available through the subclass 190 visa — permanent nomination.
He found state and territory nomination criteria varying — each jurisdiction setting its own list.
State nomination adds five points to the points test score — significant in competitive rounds.
She found state nomination requiring registration through the state's skilled migration portal.
He found state nomination requiring evidence of genuine intention to settle in the state.
State nomination through the subclass 491 is regional — she was required to live regionally for three years.
She describes state nomination as the mechanism that most accelerated her permanent residency pathway.

words.meaning: bölgesel vize (kırsal alanlara yerleşimi teşvik eden)
sentences: She accepted a regional visa knowing she would need to live outside of Sydney — she chose Geelong.
He found regional visas offering faster processing and extra points to attract migrants to regional areas.
A regional visa requires the applicant to live and work in a designated regional area of Australia.
She found the subclass 491 the most common regional skilled visa.
He found regional visa holders eligible to apply for permanent residency after three years.
Regional visas in Australia are part of a broader strategy to distribute population growth beyond capital cities.
She found regional areas broadly defined — including many cities outside Sydney, Melbourne, and Brisbane.
He found regional visa living conditions varying enormously — from large regional cities to remote towns.
Regional visas can be sponsored by a state or territory, or by an eligible relative in a regional area.
She describes her regional visa years as the most unexpectedly rewarding chapter of her Australian life.
She found integration the most personal and uneven part of the migration experience.
He found integration requiring both the migrant and the host community to meet each other halfway.
Integration is the process by which migrants become full participants in their new society.
She found integration happening fastest through employment, friendships, and local community involvement.
He found integration distinct from assimilation — integration allows cultural identity to be maintained.
Integration in Australia is supported by settlement services, language programs, and community organisations.
She found integration a lifelong process — not a point she reached but a direction she continued.
He found the integration of skilled migrants into Australian workplaces still facing barriers — recognition of qualifications chief among them.
Integration outcomes improve with English proficiency, social networks, and employment.
She describes integration as the work she is most proud of — and the work she knows is never quite finished.

words.meaning: onursal Avustralyalı (topluluk tarafından kabul görmüş göçmen)
sentences: She was called an honorary Australian by her colleagues — she took it as the greatest compliment.
He found the phrase honorary Australian used warmly and affectionately by Australians welcoming a newcomer.
An honorary Australian is an informal title given to someone who has embraced Australian values and culture.
She found the honorary Australian tag applied when she started following the footy and attending the local club.
He found the honorary Australian moment different for everyone — for him it was the first barbecue he hosted.
Honorary Australian status is informal — no certificate, just belonging.
She found the honorary Australian designation more meaningful than any formal document she had received.
He found Australians generous in extending honorary Australian status — quick to include, slow to exclude.
Honorary Australian was the phrase she heard at citizenship — warm, funny, and exactly right.
She describes being called an honorary Australian as the moment she understood she had not just moved to a country — she had joined a community.
She found fair go the Australian value that most resonated with what she had been looking for.
He found Australians invoking fair go when they saw someone being treated unfairly.
Fair go is an Australian value meaning everyone deserves an equal chance — regardless of background.
She found fair go shaping Australian attitudes toward welfare, sport, and workplace relations.
He found the phrase fair go used in political debate, workplace disputes, and everyday conversation.
Fair go means not pulling someone down for their success — and not ignoring those who need a hand up.
She found fair go the concept that most explained why Australians were uncomfortable with extremes of wealth and poverty.
He found fair go instilled in Australian children through sport, school, and family culture.
Fair go is not a formal law — it is a deeply held social expectation.
She describes fair go as the two words that most summarised why she had chosen Australia — and why she was staying.
